quest.title: Farewell, Sweet Salt
quest.description: With the aid of Zhongli's knowledge, you are able to undo the seals, but before entering the ruin, he lays a condition before Wanyan and Kliment: to alternate who gets claim to each treasure encountered, with only one object permitted per claim.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x575, Mora x31125, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

talks.objective: Explore the cave and enter the ruins
Explore further and look for divine relics

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: Look at this. It's filled halfway with salt.

dialogues.speaker: Kliment
dialogues.text: Just looks like a fancy salt holder. Seems like the God of Salt was a god lacking in treasures.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: According to my knowledge, it's no ordinary vessel. Although it is only half-full, it is also forever half-full — that is to say, it is bottomless.

dialogues.speaker: Kliment
dialogues.text: What!? You're saying that even if I pour the salt out, the amount inside won't change!?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Exactly.

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: Able to produce endless salt... The God of Salt is powerful indeed!

dialogues.speaker: Kliment
dialogues.text: Finally, after all that effort, I've found precious treasure! I claim this as mine!

dialogues.speaker: Kliment
dialogues.text: I just need to pour the endless salt into a thousand, or ten-thousand bags... I can sell it and make a fortune!

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: Hey! How can you use a relic of the God of Salt for such a shallow pursuit!?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: If Mr. Kliment wants this salt chalice, then the next object we find will belong to Miss Wanyan, according to the contract agreed upon.

dialogues.speaker: Kliment
dialogues.text: Of course, as we agreed, hehe. But how can anything be worth more than this rare find?

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: Since we have a contract, it's no use for me to fight with him...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Then let's move on, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Kliment
dialogues.text: Ha, just a simple ruler. Doesn't look to be worth anything.

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: This... if I remember correctly, this is some kind of measuring tool.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Indeed. But the God of Salt imbued it with another power.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: When you stick this ruler in the ground, the surrounding area will become covered in salt, much like a rising tide covers the earth.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: The deeper it is stuck in the ground, the more salt will appear. It is essentially a "bumper harvest" of salt.

dialogues.speaker: Kliment
dialogues.text: Wh— Th—That's even better than the salt chalice!

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Well then, according to our contract, the salt ruler goes to Miss Wanyan.

dialogues.speaker: Kliment
dialogues.text: No! Unacceptable! I paid for and organized this entire expedition. Why should I get the short end of the stick?

dialogues.speaker: Kliment
dialogues.text: And this girl has been useless. Why would she get anything!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh boy, here we go again...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: So you are saying, you want to break the contract?

response.speaker: Kliment
response.text: So what if I break it? Now that I've seen how the mechanisms in this ruin work, I no longer need you.

response.speaker: Kliment
response.text: Let's not forget who hired who here. Why should I let YOU make the rules?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Because you agreed to a contract.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Rex Lapis once said: "Ones who break their contracts shall suffer the Wrath of the Rock."

response.speaker: Kliment
response.text: That is one of your Liyue gods. I am from Snezhnaya, I—

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: —Will "suffer the Wrath of the Rock" — you may find it rather unpleasant.

choices.text: While we're on the topic of "useless" people...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: I shall confiscate your treasure as well.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: You are not worthy to continue any further into the ruin. Leave this place.

dialogues.speaker: Kliment
dialogues.text: Darn you... Just you wait!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Some "archaeological survey..." He could only pretend for so long.

choices.text: At least we had our guard up.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, good thing Paimon can smell a liar from a mile away.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Kliment's wrongdoing stemmed from greed, yes. But besides greed, there are many other things that may tempt us to break contracts.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: When people see the object of their dreams, how many are really able to control their desire and follow the contract...?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I think we should be honest with each other now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Be honest about what?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: That in truth, not a single member of this "archaeological expedition" came here for archaeology.

response.speaker: Wanyan
response.text: Wh—Why do you say that?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Miss, you lack even the most basic archaeological knowledge and can recognize naught but a few simple relics. However, you are an expert when it comes to anything regarding the God of Salt.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: You aren't interested in archaeology or relics — what you're really interested in is the God of Salt.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I believe those legends about the God of Salt that you mentioned on the Pearl Galley are passed down between generations at Yinyuan Hall...

response.speaker: Wanyan
response.text: Okay, that's enough!

response.speaker: Wanyan
response.text: ...Sir, you are indeed a man of great knowledge and talents. I seem to have been right to seek you out, once I plucked up my courage.

response.speaker: Wanyan
response.text: You're right. I'm not a scholar of archaeology. I come from one of the Eight Trades under the jurisdiction of the Qixing — Yinyuan Hall of the salt industry.

response.speaker: Wanyan
response.text: Our ancestors were those protected by the God of Salt all those years ago, when the Archon War engulfed the land in chaos.

choices.text: Come to think of it, I've never heard you say "Rex Lapis..."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right. Now that you mention it, the people of Liyue very seldom use the name "Morax..."

response.speaker: Wanyan
response.text: During the war, Morax assassinated our god out of envy for her power! He left us alone and lost in the world.

response.speaker: Wanyan
response.text: We— We hate him! But this is Morax's Liyue, after all, and its history is written as he wishes...

response.speaker: Wanyan
response.text: So, I seek proof of Morax's guilt! He has blood on his hands, and cruelty in his heart!

response.speaker: Wanyan
response.text: We agreed to a contract that we will face the truth head-on, didn't we, Mr. Zhongli!? You must judge this history fairly!

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Naturally, of course. But I must add, Liyue is no longer Morax's Liyue.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Come with me. All the answers you seek lie ahead.

choices.text: Hmm, I've never heard you say "Lord of Geo..."
I hope you never become as greedy as him, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Paimon likes Mora, but Paimon doesn't do bad things!

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: This is... a sword?

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: Aha! It's a broken sword, this is proof! This proves that the God of Salt had to fight back, fight back against the evil Morax! But sadly, she was defeated...

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: The power of this sword surely is much greater than that of the salt chalice and the salt ruler!

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: If we can repair this sword, then we can show the world the mighty power of the God of Salt...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... It does look like something left behind after being defeated in battle.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Two pieces of a broken sword. From an archaeological perspective, these are two separate relics. According to the contract, you can only claim one.

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: Wh—Why? We were alternating claims to treasure, true, but Kliment is no longer here...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Yes, but the "only one object per claim" clause still holds true. You cannot take two relics at the same time.

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: Th—This logic...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Zhongli, she seems like a good person, and no one is fighting over the treasure. How about you let this one slide, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: When there's a contract, nothing can be allowed to "slide." If the contract is not followed, then it is broken.

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: No! If I only take one half, then it can't be repaired, and the power of the God of Salt cannot be restored...

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: No matter what, I must be faithful to her...

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: Even if it breaks the contract, I don't care.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: So you are already decided? Hmm... Then there is a price to pay for breaking the contract.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Zhongli!

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: That is to say, you consign yourself to "suffer the Wrath of the Rock."

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: That... that's okay. The God of Salt gave up her life to protect her people. My sacrifice is nothing compared to that.

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: Punish me however you want. Just let me take this proof of my faith!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, you can't hit her!

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: ...Perhaps that punishment would be easier for her, but...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: As punishment, I will tell you the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: The truth? You mean the truth is my punishment?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Yes. The truth that I am about to tell you shall be your price to pay for breaking the contract.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: I'm afraid to say that the God of Salt, Havria, was not the powerful god you imagine her to be.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Rather, she was a small and weak god who yielded to all other gods. When it came to war, she lost... never able to win a seat among The Seven.

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: Wh—What...!?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: During the Archon War, the gods of this world used all their strength and cunning to vie for control of Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: But Havria instead chose to flee. She thought that by giving up before a fight could start, she could save herself and her people from the war.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: However, during such a long war, there is no end to the advances of aggressors.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: After making countless concessions, Havria had lost all of her lands until only one small haven remained.

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: No... no... it can't be so...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: In her last days, she had not even a single blade to defend her people with.

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: "Not even a single blade?" Then, this sword...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: This sword is not a relic belonging to the God of Salt... but is instead the murder weapon used to kill her.

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: Murder weapon?

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: No! That's not true, that can't be true! You are trying to test my faith in the God of Salt!

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: As I said before, I only state the facts.

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: Preposterous! Y—You are a follower of Morax, don't try to trick me!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Heyyy! Come back!

choices.text: That was too much for her to take.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: It is a punishment, after all. I did not want to tell her such cruel facts, but the contract was broken...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Let's follow her deeper into the ruin. There, I fear, we will find something that will leave her no choice but to face the truth.

choices.text: What you said really is true, right?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Indeed. Otherwise, why would I use the truth as punishment? I did not want to tell her such cruel facts, but the contract was broken...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Are these statue thingies... running?

talks.objective: Talk to Wanyan and witness the truth

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: This is the scene of the crime. Havria's body dissipated, leaving nothing but these traces of salt. Her dying moments have since been frozen in time to this very day.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: The story continues that some among her people realized at last that this gentle, kind, but weak god could never protect anyone in wartime.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: The Archon War was cruel in the extreme. Instead of consigning her to the agony of defeat, they thought, perhaps it would be better to give her a quick release.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... what about these statue thingies?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: No matter how weak the god, the power that flows forth when they are slain is beyond the strength of mortal coils to bear.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Those who could not flee were thus transformed.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Those of her people who were untouched by this disaster left for Liyue, where they sought refuge with Rex Lapis.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Their descendants feared Havria's remnants and lived in terror that she had laid upon them an eternal curse...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: So they risked their lives to come here to break the sword, and offer up obeisances in hopes that her anger might be appeased.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: But they need not have done so. For how could a god who had never once resisted — even till the end — nurse hatred for her people in her heart?

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: I—I... Even if this is so, I can't...

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: This must be a lie... a false history... all of it!

dialogues.speaker: Wanyan
dialogues.text: Don't you dare try to... shake my faith!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yikes, Zhongli didn't show any mercy this time, either...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: This is the price she must pay... Yet I would not call it a bad thing.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Judging by how she appeared, I fear that she will struggle for a time. But even if she may not escape that struggle immediately, simply recognizing the truth is good enough for now.

choices.text: You seem all too familiar with what happened to the God of Salt.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Indeed. In ages past, Havria's story served as a warning to me as well.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Faith in a god who has already passed will do you no good.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: So it is for Havria, and so it is for Morax also.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The people of Liyue will understand that one day.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Alright, then. Now, would you like to accompany me in taking a trip to Guyun Stone Forest?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What do you want to do, Zhongli?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: *sigh* ...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Treading old ground, telling old stories...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: ...One cannot help but be reminded of old acquaintances.

choices.text: You didn't just hear rumors about the way to break the seal, did you?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: No, indeed. How sharp of you — yet this is not a matter of wisdom. Only age.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What will we find ahead...?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Salt. And betrayal.
